html:
Marrakesh was founded around 1070 by the Almoravids, Berber warriors of a reform movement from the Sahara, as the capital of their new empire. The name Morocco comes from it.

Under Yusuf ibn Tashfin the Almoravids ruled from the Senegal river to Spain, where they crossed in 1086 to save al-Andalus from the Christian kingdoms. The city got walls, mosques and underground water channels. In 1147 the Almohads of Ibn Tumart took it and made it their capital too, building the Kutubiyya.

Marrakesh was the capital again under the Saadis, among them Ahmad al-Mansur. Its great square, Jemaa el-Fnaa, with storytellers and musicians, and its medina are a World Heritage Site. See also Almoravids and Almohads.
